The challenge

What makes process, chemical & pharma manufacturing different.

01

Chemical enquiries arrive on marketplaces with grades, CAS numbers and packing needs that sales must interpret quickly.

02

Finished batches wait in quarantine while QA chases pending tests, open deviations and signatures across separate systems.

03

Every consignment needs the right CoA and current safety data sheet, plus the e-way bill details buyers ask for.

04

Export shipments need product-specific documents, and one HS code or batch mismatch can hold cargo at the port.

05

Any automation near GMP records raises valid concerns about data integrity and revalidation effort.

Where automation helps

Practical uses for process, chemical & pharma manufacturing.

01

Grade-aware enquiry capture

Extract product, grade, CAS number where given, quantity, packing and delivery location from marketplace and website enquiries, and route them to the right product manager.

02

Batch yield and downtime reporting

Report yield, cycle time and downtime per batch and line from ERP or MES exports, as a reporting copy that leaves batch records untouched.

03

Batch release readiness board

Read QC test, deviation and batch record review status from validated systems and remind reviewers, so planning and sales know when stock will be released.

04

GxP-aware maintenance reminders

Remind teams of preventive maintenance, calibration and statutory inspections while execution records stay in the validated CMMS or equipment logbooks.

05

Dispatch packs with CoA and SDS

Send buyers the invoice, e-way bill details, batch certificate of analysis and current safety data sheet in one dispatch update.

06

Export document checklist

Build destination and product-specific checklists, prefill invoice and packing list drafts, and catch inconsistencies before the CHA files.

Enquiry & qualificationStandard3–5 weeks

Marketplace and website enquiry capture with routing

Pull every enquiry from IndiaMART, TradeIndia, the website and the RFQ inbox into one CRM queue, remove duplicates, extract what the buyer needs and route it to the right product or territory owner with a response deadline.

Industrial & engineering manufacturers · Process, chemical & pharma manufacturing · Contract & private-label manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Enquiries arrive through marketplace dashboards, email, website forms, phone calls and trade-fair cards. Sales coordinators copy them by hand, duplicates from the same buyer go to two reps, and enquiries that arrive after hours wait until someone notices them. Buyers who send the same RFQ to several suppliers often shortlist whoever replies first with a sensible question.

Trigger

A new lead appears through the IndiaMART Lead Manager API, a marketplace or website form notification arrives, or an email lands in the shared RFQ inbox.

How it runs

  • Collect leads from the IndiaMART Lead Manager API, other marketplace notifications, website forms and the RFQ mailbox into one queue.
  • Normalize names, phone numbers, company names and GSTIN where given, then match against existing CRM accounts and open enquiries to avoid duplicate follow-up.
  • Use an AI model to extract product, grade or specification, quantity, delivery location, required date and attachments, and list missing information as questions for the rep.
  • Score fit against agreed rules such as product range, minimum order, serviceable region and buyer type, and route to the product or territory owner with a response deadline.
  • Send an acknowledgement by email, or by WhatsApp only where the buyer started the chat or opted in, and alert the owner in Slack or the CRM app.
  • Escalate enquiries with no human response by the deadline to the sales coordinator.

Human checkpoint

The sales coordinator reviews low-confidence extractions, out-of-territory enquiries and anything flagged as a large or strategic account before routing. Reps qualify every enquiry by call or email; the automation never sends prices or delivery commitments.

Systems it connects

  • IndiaMART Lead Manager API
  • TradeIndia and other B2B marketplaces
  • Website forms and RFQ mailbox
  • CRM such as Zoho CRM, HubSpot or Salesforce

Data & consent

Uses the business contact details and enquiry content the buyer submitted. Only fields needed for qualification are kept in the CRM; raw marketplace payloads are held for a short agreed period for troubleshooting, then deleted. Promotional messages go only to contacts who agreed to receive them. Access follows CRM roles.

What we deliver

  • Unified enquiry queue in the CRM
  • Extraction and routing rules with confidence thresholds
  • Response-time and source dashboard
  • Escalation alerts for unowned enquiries

How we measure it

  • Enquiry first-response time
  • Duplicate enquiry rate
  • Enquiries without an owner after the deadline
  • Qualified enquiries by source

Plan, procure, make & checkStandard4–6 weeks

Daily production and OEE-style reporting from ERP and MES data

Collect shift production, downtime and rejection entries from the ERP, MES or shift sheets, check them for gaps, and publish a plant dashboard and a short written summary in time for the morning production meeting.

Industrial & engineering manufacturers · Process, chemical & pharma manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Production figures arrive from different lines as Excel sheets, WhatsApp photos of logbooks and ERP entries made a day late. The morning meeting spends its time agreeing numbers instead of acting on them, downtime reasons are recorded inconsistently, and lines or shifts cannot be compared reliably.

Trigger

A scheduled run after each shift or at a fixed time before the morning meeting, reading the latest ERP, MES or shift sheet data.

How it runs

  • Pull shift output, planned and actual run time, downtime with reason codes, rejections and rework from ERP, MES exports or structured shift sheets.
  • Flag missing shifts, impossible values and unmapped downtime reasons to the line supervisor before the report runs.
  • Model the data in a warehouse with agreed definitions and calculate availability, performance and quality where machine and standard-rate data allow; for batch plants, report yield and cycle time per batch.
  • Publish a Power BI dashboard by plant, line, shift and product, with trends and the top downtime reasons.
  • Draft a short written summary of the main variances for the plant head, linked to the underlying numbers.

Human checkpoint

Line supervisors confirm reason codes and corrections before figures are published, and the plant head reviews the written summary and owns any action. For GxP plants the dashboard is a reporting copy; batch records in validated systems remain the record.

  • Data pipeline with completeness checks

Plan, procure, make & checkStandard4–6 weeks

Preventive maintenance alerts and breakdown logging

Generate maintenance work orders from calendar, run-hour or count schedules, remind technicians and supervisors before due dates, log breakdowns with cause and spares used, and track statutory inspection dates.

Industrial & engineering manufacturers · Process, chemical & pharma manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Preventive maintenance schedules sit in Excel or in a CMMS nobody updates. Tasks are skipped under production pressure, breakdowns are fixed without recording cause or parts, and due dates for statutory inspections of lifting equipment and pressure vessels live in one person's diary.

Trigger

A schedule threshold is reached by date, run hours or production count from MES or meter readings, or an operator reports a breakdown.

How it runs

  • Set up the asset register with maintenance plans, checklists and statutory inspection due dates agreed with the maintenance head.
  • Create work orders ahead of the due date and notify the assigned technician and supervisor, escalating tasks that become overdue.
  • Let technicians close work orders on mobile with checklist results, readings, photos and spares used.
  • Log breakdowns with symptom, cause, downtime and parts, and feed them into MTBF and MTTR reporting.
  • Remind the safety officer and the occupier's team of upcoming statutory inspections and the reports due from competent persons.

Human checkpoint

The maintenance head approves schedule changes and every deferral, and safety-critical tasks cannot be deferred without a named sign-off. For GxP equipment, calibration and maintenance records stay in the validated CMMS or logbook; this workflow only sends reminders.

Plan, procure, make & checkAdvanced5–8 weeks

Batch release readiness tracker around validated systems

Show, for every batch, whether production records, QC tests, deviations and documents are complete by reading status from validated systems, and remind the right reviewers, without touching the GxP record itself.

Process, chemical & pharma manufacturing · Contract & private-label manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Finished batches wait in quarantine while QA chases missing signatures, pending QC tests, open deviations and CoA drafts across separate systems and paper records. Planning and sales cannot tell when stock will be released, so they call QA repeatedly, and brand clients ask for status the plant cannot easily give.

Trigger

A batch is completed in the ERP or MES, or the status of a QC test, deviation or batch record review changes in its source system.

How it runs

  • Read batch status, QC test status from the LIMS, open deviations from the QMS and batch record review status through read-only exports or reports.
  • Show a readiness board per batch listing what is complete, what is pending and the responsible reviewer.
  • Send reminders to reviewers for overdue items and a daily summary of batches expected to be ready for the release decision.
  • Give planning, sales and brand clients a release-expected view without exposing GxP record content.

Human checkpoint

Only QA releases or rejects a batch, following site SOPs in the validated systems. The tracker is a read-only, non-GxP reporting layer introduced through the site's change control, and it never creates, edits or approves a GxP record or signature.

Tools

PPythonSSupabaseRRetoolnn8nSSlack

Systems it connects

  • LIMS such as LabWare or STARLIMS
  • QMS for deviations and CAPA
  • ERP or MES batch records
  • Batch record review log

Data & consent

Batch and test status data only. The tracker copies just the status fields needed for reminders, with timestamps and source references, and refreshes rather than edits them. Access is role-based, brand clients see only their own batches, and retention follows the site's document control policy.

What we deliver

  • Read-only status integration with LIMS, QMS and ERP
  • Batch readiness board
  • Reviewer reminders and daily summary
  • Release-expected view for planning and clients

How we measure it

  • Batch completion to release time
  • Batches waiting on a single pending item
  • Overdue review items
  • Release date queries to QA

Invoice, dispatch & deliverStandard3–5 weeks

Dispatch updates with invoice, e-way bill and documents

When an order is invoiced and dispatched, send the buyer the invoice, e-way bill number, transporter and vehicle details, plus the CoA and safety data sheet where needed, and alert the dispatch team before an e-way bill expires in transit.

Distributors & dealer networks · Process, chemical & pharma manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Buyers and dealers call the sales rep to ask whether goods have left, which transporter is carrying them and when they will arrive. Dispatch teams forward invoice photos on WhatsApp, certificates of analysis are emailed separately, and e-way bills sometimes lapse on delayed consignments because nobody is watching validity.

Trigger

The ERP marks an invoice as posted with an IRN and e-way bill number, or the transporter updates the lorry receipt or vehicle number.

How it runs

  • Read invoice number, IRN status, e-way bill number and validity, transporter, vehicle number and LR details from the ERP or GSP integration.
  • Check for gaps such as missing Part B vehicle details, values that differ between invoice and e-way bill, or missing batch documents, and alert dispatch before the truck leaves.
  • Attach the invoice and, for chemical and pharma shipments, the batch certificate of analysis released by QC and, for hazardous products, the current safety data sheet from the regulatory or EHS owner.
  • Send an approved dispatch template to the buyer's opted-in contacts with document links and the expected delivery window.
  • Watch e-way bill validity against transit status, alert the dispatch lead and transporter before the extension window opens, and capture proof of delivery from the transporter.

Human checkpoint

The dispatch lead handles every exception; vehicle changes and e-way bill extensions are made in the e-way bill system by the dispatch team or the transporter carrying the goods. The automation never generates, cancels or extends e-invoices or e-way bills; it reads status and alerts people. Only QC releases CoAs.

Invoice, dispatch & deliverStandard4–6 weeks

Export documentation checklist for chemical and pharma shipments

For each export order, build the document checklist by destination, incoterm and product, prefill drafts from ERP data, check consistency across documents and track every item through to the shipping bill and bill of lading.

Process, chemical & pharma manufacturing

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Chemical and pharma exports need a long, product-specific set of documents: commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, certificates of analysis, safety data sheets, dangerous goods declarations and buyer-specific regulatory papers. Errors in HS codes, quantities or consignee details cause port delays and payment disputes, and status lives in email threads with the CHA.

Trigger

An export sales order is confirmed in the ERP, or a booking confirmation arrives from the freight forwarder.

How it runs

  • Generate a checklist from rules for the destination, incoterm, product class and buyer requirements, with an owner and due date for each document.
  • Prefill the commercial invoice and packing list from the ERP, and attach the batch CoA, safety data sheet and LUT reference for exports made without payment of IGST.
  • Check HS code, quantities, weights, values, batch numbers and consignee details for consistency across all documents and highlight mismatches.
  • Share the draft set with the CHA and freight forwarder, and track shipping bill, certificate of origin and bill of lading status.
  • Remind finance to track export realization once the shipping bill and bill of lading are received.

Human checkpoint

The export documentation executive verifies every document before release. HS and dangerous goods classification and regulatory documents are decided by the trade compliance or regulatory owner, and the CHA files the shipping bill. The automation never submits a filing.

  • LIMS or QC document store
